messages.content: Predict a human choice in an anonymous two-person resource-allocation experiment. Player V is the first mover and starts with€3; player R starts with€10. These are neutral role labels, not a claim that the participant is a prisoner. V chooses ignore or challenge. If V ignores, payoffs are€3 to V and€10 to R. If V challenges, R may yield or resist. Yield gives€10 to V and€3 to R. Challenge followed by resistance leads to a competitive wall sit: both simultaneously bend their knees against a wall, with thighs parallel to the floor, and the person who endures longer wins€6; the loser gets€0. Higher past grades indicate endurance, but do not guarantee the outcome of the later competitive sit. The local record does not specify the tie-payment rule. Before these choices everyone completed two individual wall sits wearing a sleeping mask and ear protectors, in groups of4–8 whose individual times were concealed. Each session ends after at most6minutes. The first, veiled sit paid€0.02per second; later game details had not yet been disclosed. Its within-session longest third received gradeA, middle thirdB, shortest thirdC. Everyone then learned their grade and the game rules, and did an unpaid unveiled sit. The second grade uses the first sit’s grade time ranges, so second grades need not be equally frequent. Each person knows their own two grades. There are three information conditions. NI:V receives neither grade of R. S:V receives R’s second-sit grade as a signal. s+S:V receives that signal plus a sign from R’s first-sit grade; firstgradeA/C staysA/C, while firstgradeB becomes displayedA or C with equal0.5probability. R knows the information rule, but never receives information about the specific V’s grades. Both roles are elicited by the strategy method before actual matching and feedback. First everyone makes one R decision for the contingency of being challenged; later they make V decisions:one inNI,three inS(one per signal),six ins+S(one per signA/C and signalA/B/C). These are contingent decisions, not successive realized encounters. The condition order for V is randomized across sessions. All V prompts are answered, even conditions not ultimately paid. After all choices, random anonymous within-session matching and a randomly selected role/decision determine payment. Outcomes and any competitive sit occur at a follow-up a few days later. No prior realized game outcomes are available during the strategy choices. A show-up fee exists but its amount is not recorded. The target is one R decision conditional on a challenge. Output only resist or yield.

You are answering as R in conditions+S. Your own veiled grade isA; your own unveiled grade isB. If later selected as R, V will see your unveiled signalB plus your veiled signA. The specific V’s grades and intended choice are unobserved. You are deciding in advance what to do if challenged, not reacting to a challenge already observed. Predict resist or yield. Your recorded stable attributes:age24years,height168cm,weight57kg. These source measurements have no exported collection time and are treated as self-known stable attributes. Belief reports, later questionnaire answers and follow-up outcomes are not supplied.
